newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New NZ wholesale electricity charging plan mulled.
newsitem.headline: New NZ wholesale electricity charging plan mulled.

text.p: A new system for charging service provider fees in New Zealand's wholesale electricity market could be put to the vote by May, Electricity Market Company (EMCO) chief executive Lincoln Gould said on Tuesday.

"It is true that some participants have left the market because of the current regime of fixed and variable charges for service providers," Gould told a Wellington conference on the wholesale electricity market.

He said a working group, established to look at the current methodology of charging fees, would this week consider a set of draft recommendations reached at a meeting last week. The recommendations will then go to a rules committee.
Gould said the recommendations were based on lowering the fixed charge "very considerably, to a fairly nominal level".

In addition, there would be a small nodal account charge so service providers paid a small fee for the number of nodes they use, and a much higher recovery of the charges based on a mega-watt variable charge.
Presently, 25 percent of charges are fixed, 25 percent are based on grid exit points, and 50 percent are variable.
"From my own personal point of view...the people who use the marketplace most should pay most, and the people who use it less should pay less," Gould said.
"We've got the working group to almost that point. We've still got to go through the voting and so on, but I think that will be a major step forward."
